steps.text: Run /mcp inside Claude Code to confirm it connected.
Customize > Connectors > + Add > Add custom connector. Name: CommuteScout. URL: https://mcp.commutescout.com/mcp. Sign-in: No sign in.
Add a request header named Authorization with the value Bearer cs_live_... (your key).
On Team and Enterprise plans, an owner adds it first under Organization settings > Connectors. The connector also appears in Claude Desktop and the mobile apps.

Add to its mcp_config.json (MCP settings > view raw config):

steps.code: codex mcp add commutescout --url https://mcp.commutescout.com/mcp --bearer-token-env-var COMMUTESCOUT_API_KEY

gemini mcp add --transport http commutescout https://mcp.commutescout.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer cs_live_..."

steps.text: Not yet. The hosted server needs an API key sent as a request header, and ChatGPT's custom MCP servers (chatgpt.com: Plugins > + > Add custom MCP server, URL https://mcp.commutescout.com/mcp) offer sign-in (OAuth) or no authentication, not a header.
Until CommuteScout supports OAuth sign-in, use a client that can send a header (any other client on this page), or the REST API from your own code.
Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.commutescout.com/mcp: stateless, no OAuth sign-in. Send the key on every request as Authorization: Bearer cs_live_... (or X-API-Key: cs_live_...).
